idiom_name: constructor/property injection of services; AsyncLocal<T> for flow-scoped values
implementation_notes: In .NET the relay appears in the class layer as constructors that take a dependency only to hand it to a collaborator, and in UI layers as component parameters. The framework answer is constructor injection: the container supplies the dependency where it is used at the composition root, so intermediates never see it; for per-request values with no natural injection point, `AsyncLocal<T>` (System.Threading) flows the value through async calls in the same execution context. Keep an explicit constructor parameter when the dependency is genuinely local - it stays visible in the signature and needs no container.
pitfalls: `AsyncLocal<T>` flows with the async execution context: a mutation inside a child context (a queued task, another thread) does not propagate back, and a value set in a long-lived scope can outlive the request.
Constructor injection hides the dependency from the call site, so a class whose constructor takes ten services is a relay (or a god object) even though no parameter is forwarded.

variants.name: Blazor cascading values in the component tree
variants.implementation_notes: In Blazor the component-tree relay is replaced by `<CascadingValue Value=...>` on an ancestor and `[CascadingParameter]` on any descendant: the renderer walks the tree instead of intermediate Razor components forwarding the parameter. Cascading values can be named and fixed (`IsFixed`) for efficiency, and they re-render consumers of an unfixed value when it changes - so wrap only the subtree that needs them.
variants.code_sketch:
<CascadingValue Value="@currentUser">
    <Router AppAssembly="typeof(App).Assembly" />
</CascadingValue>

@code {
    [CascadingParameter] public User? CurrentUser { get; set; }
}
pitfalls: A cascading value that is never provided yields the parameter's default (usually null) instead of erroring; guard it explicitly or throw in the consumer.
Cascading values are per render tree, not per DI scope: they are not a replacement for container-registered services and they re-render consumers when an unfixed value changes.
